rules.good: df.limit(10_000).toPandas(), aggregate first, or df.writeTo("<catalog>.<schema>.<table>").createOrReplace() and read it with SQL
rules.why: the whole result lands in the 1 GiB driver heap; above 512 MiB the call fails

rules.good: write the data to a table once (writeTo), then spark.table(...)
rules.why: local data is shipped inside every task of every job

rules.bad: a Python loop that runs one job per item
rules.good: one query with a join or groupBy, or df.repartition(n) plus mapInPandas
rules.why: every job adds a broadcast and a plan to the driver

rules.good: from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast; df.join(broadcast(small_df), ...) once, outside the loop
rules.why: one broadcast instead of one per iteration

rules.good: df.unpersist() when done; cache only what several actions reuse
rules.why: cached blocks occupy executor memory, 1 GiB each, and are not freed by themselves

rules.bad: pd.read_csv(chunksize=250_000) then spark.createDataFrame(chunk) + saveAsTable(append) per chunk
rules.good: chunks of at most 20_000 rows (about 1 MiB per task), finished chunk numbers in a small table so a restart can resume, and see stardelt/stardelt#52 for the planned loader
rules.why: measured 2026-10-21: 250_000 rows = tasks of 11 MiB, 305 warnings in 3 h, driver OOMKilled

rules.good: run it once, keep the number
